answer.text: Establishing, developing, and regulating pension funds and the National Pension System (NPS)
Setting interest rates for bank deposits

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XV page 259, PFRDA is the pension-sector regulator that acts under the PFRDA Act, 2013. It was constituted in October 2003 and is responsible for promoting old age income security by establishing, developing and regulating pension funds, and for designing the structure of funds and constituents in the NPS. The Trap: PFRDA specifically covers the pension sector — not stock exchanges, foreign exchange reserves, or bank deposit rates. Note: Distinguish carefully — PFRDA acts under the PFRDA Act, 2013, but the Authority itself was constituted earlier, in October 2003.
